passage: India's forest management system classifies lands into three categories to ensure ecological stability. Reserved forests are the most strictly regulated, where all activities are prohibited unless specifically permitted for local community needs. Unlike the misconception that these are for government officials, they are managed to prevent over-exploitation and maintain forest health. Furthermore, conservation efforts like Project Tiger have evolved significantly. While initially focused on preventing poaching, the program now prioritizes the protection of entire habitats to ensure the survival of the species within their natural ecosystem. This shift recognizes that a tiger cannot survive without a healthy forest environment. Similarly, many local communities protect patches of forest known as sacred groves. These areas are not merely preserved for their medicinal plants, as some believe, but are protected due to deep-rooted cultural and religious beliefs that view the entire forest as a sacred entity. By protecting these groves, communities inadvertently preserve biodiversity, including rare species that might otherwise disappear. These conservation strategies, ranging from strict government regulation to community-led initiatives, are essential for maintaining the delicate balance of India's wildlife resources and ensuring that ecosystems remain resilient against human-induced pressures.

items.evidence: Reserved forests are the most strictly regulated, where all activities are prohibited unless specifically permitted for local community needs.
items.q: A villager wants to graze cattle in a reserved forest. When may this be allowed?
options: Only if permitted for local community needs
Never, since only officials may enter
Always, as protected forests allow grazing
Only if the forest is not yet surveyed
items.explain: Reserved forests prohibit all activities unless specifically permitted for local community needs.

wrong.why: thinks reserved forests are only for officials
mixes up reserved and protected forest rules
thinks forest class depends on being surveyed

items.evidence: This shift recognizes that a tiger cannot survive without a healthy forest environment.
items.q: Why did Project Tiger begin to protect whole habitats and not only tigers?
options: Tigers need a healthy forest to survive
The forests were meant for officials
Tigers could be bred outside forests
items.explain: A tiger cannot survive without a healthy forest, so protecting the habitat protects the species.

wrong.why: thinks the project only fought hunting
thinks forests are mainly for officials
assumes tigers can live without forests

items.evidence: These areas are not merely preserved for their medicinal plants, as some believe, but are protected due to deep-rooted cultural and religious beliefs that view the entire forest as a sacred entity.
items.q: Why does a village protect even the plants in a sacred grove that have no medicinal use?
options: They see the whole forest as sacred
Only rare herbs there are valued
The government pays them to guard it
Only the largest trees are sacred
items.explain: Communities protect sacred groves because their beliefs treat the entire forest as sacred, not just medicinal plants.

wrong.why: thinks groves are protected only for medicinal plants
thinks only big trees count as sacred

items.evidence: By protecting these groves, communities inadvertently preserve biodiversity, including rare species that might otherwise disappear.
items.q: What would likely happen to rare species if a community stopped guarding its grove?
options: They might disappear from that forest
They would be safe, as hunting is the only danger
They would move to a reserved forest
They would stay safe, as forests need no care
items.explain: Protected groves preserve rare species that might otherwise disappear, so without protection they could be lost.

wrong.why: assumes species relocate on their own
